package_info.why_malicious: The package is not overtly malicious in the traditional sense (e.g., credential theft, code execution), but it abuses the npm registry by programmatically publishing thousands of versions in a short period using an automated script. This behavior is considered registry pollution and can be used for denial-of-service, squatting, or other disruptive purposes. The presence of an automated publishing script (upload.ps1) is the core indicator of this abuse.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When manually executed, the script repeatedly generates new package.json files with incremented version numbers and publishes them to the npm registry in an infinite loop, resulting in mass version spamming.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automating the publication of thousands of package versions serves no legitimate development purpose and is disruptive to the npm ecosystem.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages are published infrequently and only when meaningful changes are made. This script intentionally floods the registry with meaningless versions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated publishing scripts are sometimes used in CI/CD pipelines for legitimate versioning, but never at this scale or frequency.
key_indicators: No meaningful code changes between versions

attack_chain.action: The upload.ps1 script is executed, starting an infinite loop.
attack_chain.leads_to: Automated generation of new package.json files with incremented versions.

attack_chain.action: Each new package.json is published to the npm registry as a new version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Massive version spamming in the npm registry.

attack_chain.action: The npm registry is polluted with thousands of meaningless package versions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential registry performance issues, confusion, and resource exhaustion.

behavioral_signatures: Automated scripts that generate and publish new package versions in a loop
Unusually high frequency of version publication for a single package
No meaningful code changes between versions
file_indicators: upload.ps1 or similar scripts in package root
package.json files with only version number changes
network_indicators: Excessive npm publish requests from a single source
Unusual npm registry activity patterns (thousands of versions in short time)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with an unusually high number of versions published in a short time frame, especially when accompanied by automation scripts (e.g., upload.ps1) in the repository. Flag packages where version increments occur without substantive code changes. Detect and alert on repeated npm publish operations from the same package with only version number changes.
